patterns.name: US pushes AI compute to stay inside its borders
patterns.line: Trump threatened a 'tremendous tax' on US firms building data centres abroad, a day after Commerce's licence rule on advanced chips. Separately today, lawmakers released records of about 880,000 approved AI chip sales.
patterns.why: If enforced, US tech firms lose cheaper or less-opposed overseas sites. Host countries such as Canada or Finland lose projects. Chinese firms lose rental routes. Enforcement is unclear.
patterns.watch: Whether Trump's tax becomes a formal order or bill, and which firms it names.

patterns.name: Nvidia faces probes over China chip diversion and accounting
patterns.line: After CEO Jensen Huang resigned, California subpoenaed Nvidia over whether chips reached China, and the SEC is reportedly probing its accounting. Huang is due before congressional committees on 1 December.
patterns.why: Investors punish the firm for disclosure risk, not just demand. Export enforcement now runs through securities law, so misleading investors about China exposure becomes a liability for chipmakers.

patterns.name: AI stocks sell off even after Anthropic's IPO
patterns.line: The Nasdaq erased all 2026 gains and closed 5% below 1 January, with about $4tn lost this week. Anthropic fell 9% to $88.30, near its $83 IPO price. Nvidia fell 14%.
patterns.why: Investors doubt returns on AI spending. Analysts also say the IPO drained cash from other tech names. Rate-hike fears lifted the dollar to a 19-month high.
patterns.watch: Whether Anthropic holds above its $83 IPO price.

patterns.name: El Niño drought hits India's farms and industry
patterns.line: Monsoon rain fell 12.6% short, and 52.5% of India's land was dry or in drought by mid-September. Separately, El Niño water shortages are straining pharma and data centres, while rural job-guarantee work halved.
patterns.why: Rural incomes and food costs take the first hit, and industrial water costs follow. INCOIS expects El Niño to last to March, with La Niña possibly lifting the 2027 monsoon.
patterns.watch: Whether states restore job-guarantee work through the rabi season.

takeaways.line: Russia's missile strike coinciding with European troop drills tests NATO's response. Article 5 needs political consensus, so the risk is miscalculation rather than a deliberate attack.
The sentence strengthens US pressure on India over alleged plots against Sikh separatists. Gupta's co-accused Vikash Yadav remains uncharged in custody terms, so the case stays open.

money.line: Robotics startup raised $500 million, per WSJ (source unreachable — headline only).

lead.headline: Independent mathematicians say the AI-built Riemann hypothesis proof is almost certainly sound
lead.hook: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says Claude proved the Riemann hypothesis, and independent mathematicians now say the proof is almost certainly correct.
points: The hypothesis, posed in 1859, says a hidden pattern governs how prime numbers (divisible only by themselves and 1) are spread out.
Alpöge wrote the proof in Lean, a programming language; a proof that compiles without errors is usually taken as logically valid.
MIT's Andrew Sutherland and others compiled it independently without issues. Sutherland says the chance of anything fishy is 'approximately zero'.
One check remains: a 'comparator run' to confirm the code does not redefine the statement or exploit a Lean bug. It typically takes hours.
Kevin Buzzard of Imperial College London said the first question is whether the Lean statement matches the real theorem.

frontpage.headline: Russian missiles land in Poland during European military drills nearby
frontpage.hook: Two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland on Friday, and NATO chief Mark Rutte called it a 'grave violation' of Polish airspace.
points: A Kh-101 cruise missile landed about 30 miles from the Ukraine border; a likely jet-powered drone hit about 20 miles from it. No injuries or damage were reported.
One missile crashed about 22 miles from European drills for a possible postwar Ukraine mission; the two-week exercise began Nov. 9. PM Donald Tusk called it an intentional provocation.
Article 5 (attack on one ally is an attack on all 32) is not automatic and needs a political decision. Poland can invoke Article 4, which gives emergency consultations only.
The same night Russia hit Ukraine with a major barrage that killed at least eight. Putin says he will treat European troops in Ukraine as legitimate targets.
UK defence intelligence chief Matthew Jones said Russia does not seek war with NATO but he fears a significant miscalculation.

frontpage.headline: Nasdaq wipes out 2026 gains as AI sell-off hits Anthropic's second day
frontpage.hook: The Nasdaq closed 5% below its 1 January level on Friday, erasing all 2026 gains, as about $4tn of market value vanished this week.
points: Anthropic fell 9% to $88.30, near its $83 IPO price, after a 17% jump on day one. Nvidia fell 14%; SanDisk fell 14% and Micron 12%.
Asian markets had their worst week since 2020. Taiwan fell 6.7%, Kospi 5.5% and Nikkei 5%. SoftBank fell 14.5%.
An IG analyst says the IPO may be draining liquidity as investors sell other shares to fund purchases of Anthropic.
Investors question whether AI spending will earn the returns to justify it. Nvidia also fell after California's subpoena.
Rate-hike fears lifted the dollar to a 19-month high. Bitcoin fell below $60,000 for the first time since early July.
frontpage.evidence_of: AI stocks sell off even after Anthropic's IPO

frontpage.headline: Trump threatens a ban and a 'tremendous tax' on US firms building AI data centres abroad
frontpage.hook: Donald Trump said he will stop US companies building AI data centres overseas and tax those that do, giving almost no detail.
points: He said 'China will take all of them'. He admitted he had not yet told his own officials.
It is unclear how it would be enforced. Meta, Google and Anthropic have overseas or Canadian data-centre deals.
He singled out Google's Finland project (€13bn investment); work on two of its centres was halted last month over forest clearance.
It follows Monday's licence rule for buying advanced chips, aimed at Chinese firms renting computing power abroad.
Data centres were a midterm issue: Democrats promising tougher rules won on 3 November. There are about 3,000 US data centres, with 1,500 more planned.
frontpage.evidence_of: US pushes AI compute to stay inside its borders

frontpage.headline: Indian man gets 19 years in US for plot to kill Sikh separatist
frontpage.hook: Nikhil Gupta, 55, was sentenced to 235 months in a New York federal court for a murder-for-hire plot against Sikh separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun.
points: Gupta pleaded guilty in February to murder-for-hire, conspiracy and money-laundering conspiracy. Prosecutors had sought about 24 years.
He arranged $15,000 in cash with Indian official Vikash Yadav for a 'hitman' who was an undercover US officer. Yadav is charged but not in US custody.
India denies involvement and says such a plot is against government policy.
Gupta was arrested in Prague and has been held since extradition in June 2023. He faces deportation after his term.
Pannun called Gupta 'a foot soldier' of Narendra Modi's government and says he will keep campaigning.

frontpage.headline: India's core industry output rises 10.9% in October, fastest in new series
frontpage.hook: Core sector output rose 10.9% in October, against 0.8% a year earlier and 8.2% in September.
points: Iron ore rose 26.4%, coal 23.1%, electricity 21.6% and cement 15.4%. Natural gas fell 7.6%, crude oil 4.1% and fertiliser 12.2%.
April–October growth was 6%, against 2.3% a year earlier. The new series has a 2022-23 base and adds iron ore as a ninth sector.
ICRA's Aditi Nayar says a low base from the shifted festive calendar flattered the number. Cement has grown double digits for four months.
She expects growth to cool to mid-single digits in November because of more holidays.

frontpage.headline: Russia fires over 400 drones and 110 missiles at Ukraine in one night
frontpage.hook: Russia fired more than 400 drones and over 110 missiles, 27 of them ballistic, at Ukraine overnight, one of the war's biggest attacks.
points: Zelenskyy says missiles came in waves 20–30 minutes apart, hampering rescue crews. Targets included Dnipro bridges, railways and power lines linked to nuclear plants.
Ukraine shot down 79 cruise missiles. Ballistic missiles are much harder to stop and depend on partner supplies.
He asked partners to speed air defence deliveries, including PAC-2 and PAC-3 missiles, and wants the Pentagon to release expected deliveries.
He says Putin ordered the attack to offset diplomatic and military setbacks.

frontpage.headline: SEC is probing Nvidia's accounting practices, Reuters reports
frontpage.hook: The US Securities and Exchange Commission is probing Nvidia's accounting practices, according to two people briefed on the matter, Reuters reports (summary from limited source text).
points: Reuters's exclusive by Chris Prentice and Alexandra Alper, dated Nov 20, says the SEC is looking at the company's accounting.
The snippets do not give details of what is being examined or the scope.
frontpage.evidence_of: Nvidia faces probes over China chip diversion and accounting

frontpage.headline: As drought grips half of India, rural job guarantee work falls by half
frontpage.hook: Rural job-guarantee work fell nearly 50% in July, to 7.67 crore person-days from 15.33 crore a year earlier, as drought covered 52.5% of India's land.
points: June–September rain was 759.4 mm against an average of 868.6 mm, 12.6% short. Dry or drought land rose from 38.9% to 52.5% in a month.
On 1 July the scheme moved from MGNREGS to the new VB-Gram G framework. Households getting work fell over 51%; July–September person-days were 284 million against 418 million.
Work per household fell from 43.2 days in 2025-26 to 17 so far this year. Economists cite pause periods and Aadhaar checks removing duplicates.
Activists say officials in Rajsamand were told not to accept applications, so unmet demand goes unrecorded. Farmers are selling livestock in distress.
El Niño is expected to last through February 2027. The author urges suspending pause periods, giving receipts for applications and an independent review.
frontpage.evidence_of: El Niño drought hits India's farms and industry

stories.headline: METR update: AI keeps improving, but still weak on judgment tasks
stories.hook: METR's updated time-horizon plot finds AI progress still exponential on checkable tasks, but models fall short on judgment-heavy work.
points: The original plot showed the task length frontier models can complete doubling every four months. Task difficulty is measured by how long humans take.
The update adds longer and more open-ended tasks. In one, models design AI evaluations; none was good enough for METR staff to find useful.
Models also fell short of humans at scoring philosophical arguments. Opus 5.5 reaches 'borderline above the bar' on evaluation design; a year ago all models were 'clearly below'.
Reinforcement learning works where success is automatically verifiable, which is why coding and maths are strong. Hard-to-verify tasks resist this.
Most human completion times are estimates, since paying people for hundred-hour tasks is too costly. Few such tasks are included, so extrapolation is hard.

stories.headline: Signal blocks screenshots to stop AI agents reading private chats
stories.hook: Signal will block screenshots on iOS 27 and supported Android versions, calling OS-level AI agents an 'existential threat' to privacy.
points: Agents such as Apple's Siri AI and Google's Gemini Intelligence can read the screen, pulling decrypted messages out of Signal's encrypted environment.
Reuters reported Meta's Muse agent accessed Signal chats on Android and macOS using broad permissions granted at setup. Meta says users explicitly grant those permissions.
Signal blocked Microsoft's Recall last year. It calls its protections incomplete: macOS screenshots can't be reliably blocked, and notifications and file access remain open.
It wants Apple, Google and Microsoft to let apps opt out of AI agents entirely and to disclose what agents access.

stories.headline: SEBI studies an India-built AI model for securities regulation
stories.hook: SEBI is studying a domestically governed AI model for the securities market, with no timeline, chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said at a Mumbai summit.
points: A committee is checking whether it could be built jointly with market participants, possibly as part of India's Digital Public Infrastructure.
The aim is to make AI regulatory tools cheaper and more accessible for smaller intermediaries.
The committee is also weighing costs, data security and safeguards against hallucinations (incorrect AI outputs).

SEBI already uses AI tools to monitor intermediaries' advertisements and compliance reports. Separately, Pandey said a paper to align FPI norms with global norms is coming; companies raised about Rs 9 lakh crore in FY27 so far.

stories.headline: Nvidia nears $500M-plus deal for diffusion-model startup Inception
stories.hook: Nvidia is nearing a deal to buy two-year-old AI startup Inception for at least $500 million, The Information reports citing three people.
points: Inception builds language models using diffusion, which refines a full response step by step rather than token by token.
The deal would bolster Nvidia's open-source Nemotron models and robot models. Palantir and US agencies use Nemotron as an alternative to Chinese models.
It includes performance bonuses for the 30-plus employees. Co-founders Stefano Ermon, Aditya Grover and Volodymyr Kuleshov are expected to join Nvidia.
Talks began before Jensen Huang's resignation and after Microsoft expressed interest.

also.line: OpenAI tightened safeguards against extraction of reasoning from GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol; internal tests show attack success down from 54.0% on GPT-6 Astra to 0.2%.
US lawmakers released confidential licensing records showing Washington approved sales of nearly 880,000 advanced AI chips, adding turmoil to Nvidia and cross-border chip trade.
Two teams independently calculate that quantum effects could make gravity repel; a post-selection measurement could show it with bacterium-sized objects, though tests would be very difficult.
KKR bought a minority stake in Gentari Renewables India, which has about 8 GW of operating, under-construction and contracted capacity; Gentari keeps operational control.

stories.headline: Big pharma says AI cuts preclinical drug discovery time by up to half
stories.hook: Executives at Novartis, AstraZeneca, GSK, Sanofi and others say AI has cut preclinical drug discovery time by as much as 50%.
points: Sanofi saved at least a year on asthma drug lunsekimig by skipping an intermediate dose-selection trial.
Novartis cut target-to-candidate time from three years to 18–24 months. Novo Nordisk cut design cycles from eight to three and lead optimisation from 64 weeks to 12.
Developing a medicine still averages 10–15 years with about 90% clinical failure. Of 129 AI-enabled drugs in trials, only 24 have completed Phase 2 and 5 reached Phase 3.
Anthropic runs a wet lab and bought two biotech startups; Novartis's CEO sits on its board.

stories.headline: La Niña may help India's 2027 monsoon after El Niño, INCOIS says
stories.hook: INCOIS expects El Niño to stay dominant until March, then fade to neutral, with rising chances of La Niña during the 2027 monsoon.
points: La Niña is El Niño's cooler counterpart, which could support the 2027 Southwest Monsoon.
The forecast is gradual: El Niño continues strengthening now, then transitions to neutral conditions after March.
stories.evidence_of: El Niño drought hits India's farms and industry

stories.headline: India's weak monsoon and El Niño expose industry's water problem
stories.hook: Water shortages linked to El Niño are hitting pharma and data centres in southern India, pushing firms to conserve and recycle (summary from limited source text).
points: Nikkei reports shortages could limit growth in industries such as textiles.
Higher costs are raising pressure to increase recycling.
stories.evidence_of: El Niño drought hits India's farms and industry

stories.headline: Yes Bank's AI-attack safeguards delay fintech payouts
stories.hook: Yes Bank's cybersecurity upgrades are delaying settlements at payment providers, after RBI told banks to tighten defences following the SBI data leak in October, per Inc42's sources.
points: Yes Bank is changing its banking APIs, delaying settlements for businesses that rely on them.
Coinbase India paused withdrawals and partly resumed; CoinDCX and Zebpay report slow payouts; Razorpay briefly delayed merchant settlements.
CERT-In warned that attackers use AI to alter business records or approval relationships and push fraudulent payments through legitimate processes at bank technology vendors.
Its listed techniques include parallel AI agents for reconnaissance and rapid exploit changes. It told banks to reconcile vendor data and restrict admin accounts.

stories.headline: Indian retail investors rush into Anthropic shares after Nasdaq debut
stories.hook: Anthropic was about 40% of INDmoney's international activity on debut day, with average orders twice the platform norm.
points: On Vested it was 11% of traded value and 9% of trades; 84% of its trades came in the first two hours. Average buy order was $1,100.
On Mudrex, 35% of daily active users traded it.
Shares opened at $111.50 against the $83 IPO price and closed at $97.17. Indian buyers pay the market price, not the IPO price, since they can't subscribe through these platforms.
The $81.3bn IPO valued Anthropic at about $1.5tn, nearly 37% of India's projected FY27 GDP of $4.06tn, though valuation and GDP measure different things.
stories.evidence_of: AI stocks sell off even after Anthropic's IPO

also.line: Indian startups raised $205.5 million across 18 rounds in the week to Nov 20, 8.5% above last year, led by Style Union ($52M), Humyn Labs ($26M) and Bharat Semi ($24M).

stories.headline: Andhra Pradesh offers up to 80% support for silicon fabs
stories.hook: Andhra Pradesh will combine with Union support to cover up to 80% of eligible capital costs for silicon fabs, 40% from each government.
points: Compound semiconductor, photonics, sensor, discrete and display fabs and advanced packaging get up to 70% combined; legacy packaging up to 50%.
OSAT and ATMP (chip assembly, testing and packaging) units get a 4.5% of net sales state incentive on top of the Union's 9%, totalling 13.5%, capped at Rs 180 crore per company.
Machinery and materials get 18% from the state plus the Union's 30%, or 48%. R&D and talent get 25% from the state, combined cap 75%.
The state plans a 5,000-acre semiconductor park in Tirupati and a research centre starting at IIT Tirupati. The policy runs five years.

stories.headline: Anthropic is among the most-traded stocks for Indian retail investors
stories.hook: Anthropic accounted for about 11% of traded value on Vested after listing at $111.50, roughly ₹10,400.
points: Vested says 20% of active traders bought it; average buy was about ₹1 lakh. INDmoney says 40% of order volume was Anthropic.
It closed at $97.17, up 17.07% from the issue price. AMD led Vested's traded value and Nvidia was third.
A Capwise founder says early moves reflect flows more than fundamentals, with the real test at first quarterly results and lock-in expiry.
Vested's CEO says Anthropic offers direct exposure to AI models, not just chips.
stories.evidence_of: AI stocks sell off even after Anthropic's IPO

also.line: RBI's new FEMA export rules, in force since 1 October, require service exporters to file an Export Declaration Form declaring full value; RBI has issued FAQs on exemptions and thresholds.

stories.headline: Congress proposes four-point delimitation formula, says INDIA bloc agrees
stories.hook: Congress wants the Lok Sabha kept at 543 seats, with state-wise distribution unchanged, one-third (182) reserved for women, and all frozen for 25 years.
points: Jairam Ramesh says delimitation (redrawing seats by population) would follow the Census results early next year under Article 82, and could hurt southern states that controlled population.
He says INDIA bloc parties, including the DMK, back the formula, and accuses the government of not consulting the Opposition.
The Monsoon session has not been prorogued since 13 August, fuelling speculation about a short-notice sitting on women's reservation and delimitation.
Convening a fresh session needs at least 14 days' notice; an extended sitting needs two days.

stories.headline: India's labour codes, a year on: uneven rollout and open questions
stories.hook: Four labour codes merging 29 central laws took effect on November 21, 2025, and a year later rollout across states remains uneven.
points: Trade unions say the codes weaken collective bargaining and make retrenchment easier.
The government says they simplify regulation, extend social security and make labour more flexible.
Questions remain over the actual reach of social security and consequences for workers. Frontline has compiled its reporting.

stories.headline: India says no change on Indus Waters Treaty as Pakistani minister attends Delhi forum
stories.hook: India's foreign ministry says there is 'absolutely no change' on the Indus Waters Treaty while Pakistan's minister Musadik Malik attends an SCO forum in Delhi.
points: The treaty was suspended in 2025 after the Pahalgam attack that killed 26 people.
It is likely the first Pakistani minister invited to India since the May 2025 hostilities. The SCO Civilisation Dialogue runs 20–22 November.
Modi inaugurated it at Purana Quila. India says all SCO members were invited as usual.
Some experts see a multilateral opening to improve ties; Malik says culture has a key role.

stories.headline: California subpoenas Nvidia over whether chips reached China
stories.hook: California's attorney general subpoenaed Nvidia on Thursday, a week after CEO Jensen Huang resigned; Nvidia shares are down by a fifth, wiping almost $1tn.
points: Rob Bonta is investigating whether chips or confidential information reached China, and whether Nvidia misled investors about the risk.
Huang resigned after admitting affairs, including one with Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese spy linked to Singapore's Megaspeed. Megaspeed bought nearly $5bn of Nvidia hardware and says it is lawful.
Nvidia's chair says it will not reinstate Huang. He testifies to congressional committees on 1 December.
AMD fell almost 8% after Hunterbrook reports on China links and 'circular financing'; AMD says they misrepresent its business.
stories.evidence_of: Nvidia faces probes over China chip diversion and accounting

stories.headline: EU ban on plastic waste exports to non-OECD countries takes effect
stories.hook: An EU ban on plastic waste exports to countries outside the OECD takes effect on Saturday, 21 November (summary from limited source text).
points: It aims to curb pollution and stop the EU shifting waste-management risks abroad.

stories.headline: Nature webinar on how AI affects science careers
stories.hook: Nature's Careers team holds a 60-minute webinar on 2 December at 15:00 GMT on AI's effect on early-career science jobs.
points: It asks whether AI doing coding and basic data analysis puts graduate student, postdoc, programmer and technician roles at risk.
These roles have traditionally been stepping stones to other scientific positions.

also.line: Amateur astronomer Pavel Rabtsevich had an AI model search telescope data and, in about two weeks, it found two possible planets around a star 116 light years away; results are mixed.

stories.headline: Qualcomm and Salesforce layoffs hit India's tech job market
stories.hook: Qualcomm has reportedly begun layoffs in India that could affect more than 1,000 jobs, while Salesforce has started another round of cuts.
points: The Federal video asks whether AI is the cause and whether big tech is moving to leaner workforces.
It also covers how required skills are changing and what this means for IT professionals and fresh graduates.

also.line: H-1B visa workers are fed up and abandoning American tech jobs (source unreachable — headline only).
The 57th International Film Festival of India opens in Goa for nine days with 150-plus films from 86 countries; Spain is Country of Honour, theme 'Stories Without Borders'.
Mike D of the Beastie Boys plays an NPR Tiny Desk Concert for his album Thank You, the first solo release from any member of the group.

stories.headline: Is this the hidden cause of allergies?
stories.hook: A study in Allergy suggests allergies may start with a mitochondrial 'power failure' in barrier cells, not an overactive immune system.
points: Allergies affect up to one in three children and have risen for decades in the US.
Researchers analysed over 110 case-control cohorts with more than 3,700 allergy patients and found genes that clear damaged mitochondria less active in sufferers.
The pattern was strongest in eosinophilic esophagitis and eczema, only partial in hay fever and absent in asthma and nasal polyps.
The authors call it 'not a cure' but a logical starting point.
stories.signal: It challenges a 60-year-old assumption about allergies and shows how a cause-and-effect reversal can reframe a disease.

stories.headline: What's so important about Nvidia's chips?
stories.hook: The Atlantic examines the truth about chip smuggling and the AI race with China (summary from limited source text).
points: The snippet gives only the subtitle and no further detail.
stories.signal: It explains why Nvidia's chips are at the centre of this week's US–China fight, which links several of today's stories.
